title: Grade 11 Chemistry — Chemical Thermodynamics
description: System, surroundings, enthalpy, entropy, Gibbs free energy
subject: chemistry

questions.question: In thermodynamics, the 'system' is:
options: The portion of the universe under study
questions.explanation: System = the part of the universe under study. Surroundings = everything else. Universe = system + surroundings. An open system exchanges both matter and energy; closed system exchanges only energy; isolated system exchanges neither.

questions.question: Enthalpy (H) is defined as:
options: H = U + PV (internal energy + pressure × volume)
questions.explanation: Enthalpy H = U + PV. At constant pressure, ΔH = qₚ (heat at constant pressure). Most chemical reactions in labs occur at constant atmospheric pressure, so ΔH is the heat of reaction.

questions.question: An exothermic reaction has:
options: ΔH < 0 (negative) — heat is released to surroundings
questions.explanation: Exothermic: ΔH < 0. Products have less energy than reactants. Heat is released. Examples: combustion, neutralisation, respiration. Endothermic: ΔH > 0 (heat absorbed, products have more energy).

questions.question: Hess's Law states that the enthalpy change of a reaction is:
options: The same regardless of the pathway taken (only depends on initial and final states)
questions.explanation: Hess's Law: ΔH is a state function — independent of the path. If a reaction can be written as a series of steps, ΔH_total = ΔH₁ + ΔH₂ + ... (even for steps that can't be measured directly).

questions.question: Standard enthalpy of formation (ΔH°f) is the enthalpy change when:
options: 1 mol of compound decomposes to elements
1 mol of compound is formed from its constituent elements in their standard states
questions.explanation: ΔH°f = enthalpy change for forming 1 mole of compound from elements in their standard states (25°C, 1 atm). By definition, ΔH°f of any element in its standard state = 0.

questions.question: Entropy (S) is a measure of:
options: Disorder or randomness of a system
questions.explanation: Entropy (S) measures disorder or randomness. Higher entropy = more disorder. S increases: solid→liquid→gas; mixing; dissolving. The Second Law: entropy of the universe always increases (ΔS_universe > 0).

questions.question: Gibbs Free Energy is defined as G = H − TS. A reaction is spontaneous when:
questions.explanation: ΔG < 0: spontaneous (thermodynamically favourable). ΔG > 0: non-spontaneous. ΔG = 0: equilibrium. A reaction can be spontaneous even if ΔH > 0, provided ΔS is large enough at high T.

questions.question: The First Law of Thermodynamics states:
options: Entropy of the universe always increases
Energy cannot be created or destroyed (ΔU = q + w)
At absolute zero, entropy is zero
questions.explanation: First Law: ΔU = q + w (internal energy change = heat added + work done on system). This is energy conservation. Second Law: ΔS_universe > 0. Third Law: S = 0 at 0 K for perfect crystal.

questions.question: Bond enthalpy is the energy required to:
options: Form a bond between two atoms
Break one mole of a particular type of bond in gaseous molecules
questions.explanation: Bond enthalpy (bond dissociation energy) = energy to break 1 mole of bonds in gaseous molecules. Bond breaking = endothermic. Bond forming = exothermic. ΔH_rxn ≈ Σ(bonds broken) − Σ(bonds formed).

questions.question: Enthalpy of combustion is always:
options: Negative (exothermic — heat is released during burning)
questions.explanation: Combustion is always exothermic (ΔH < 0). The enthalpy of combustion of carbon (coal) is −393.5 kJ/mol (forms CO₂). Fuels are valued for their large negative enthalpies of combustion.

questions.question: If ΔH = −100 kJ and ΔS = −0.2 kJ/K at 300 K, is the reaction spontaneous?
questions.explanation: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS = −100 − (300)(−0.2) = −100 + 60 = −40 kJ. Since ΔG < 0, the reaction is spontaneous at 300 K.

questions.question: Lattice enthalpy is the energy required to:
options: Form 1 mole of ionic solid from its gaseous ions
Completely separate 1 mole of ionic solid into its gaseous ions
Dissolve 1 mole of salt in water
questions.explanation: Lattice enthalpy = energy to convert 1 mol ionic solid into isolated gaseous ions. It is always endothermic (large positive value). Greater lattice enthalpy = stronger ionic bond.

questions.question: An isolated system obeys: ΔU = ?
questions.explanation: An isolated system exchanges neither heat nor work with surroundings: q = 0 and w = 0. Therefore ΔU = 0. Internal energy of an isolated system is constant (First Law).

questions.question: At constant pressure, if a gas expands by ΔV, the work done BY the system is:
questions.explanation: Work done by system = PΔV (expansion, positive — system does work on surroundings). Work done on system = −PΔV. First Law: ΔU = q − PΔV (heat absorbed minus work done by system).

questions.question: The standard enthalpy of neutralisation of a strong acid with a strong base is approximately:
questions.explanation: Strong acid + strong base neutralisation: H⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → H₂O(l), ΔH ≈ −57.3 kJ/mol. This is constant because fully dissociated acids and bases, regardless of identity.
